new.n: West Prairie mill: the Holcomb brothers' dam on Tamarack Creek
new.pl: SW 1/4 NE 1/4 sec. 5 T18N R9W, Tamarack Creek, West Prairie (Trempealeau Co.)
new.v: Coins 1850s-1930s, mill and farm-trade losses, tools
new.st: History of Trempealeau County (1917): Al and Abe Holcomb, brothers who settled on West Prairie, put a dam in Tamarack Creek in sec. 5 T18N R9W and built a saw mill. They cut the logs of Holcomb Cooley, which is named for them, into lumber for the settlers. In 1917 West Prairie still had a mill, a church, a band stand, a cemetery and a school. Wisconsin DNR records list the 'West Prairie Mill' dam at this point (owner H. Wachter, 23 ft high), removed in 1937.
new.t: Work the dam ends, the mill yard below the dam and the old road to the prairie. Ask the landowner.
src: Wisconsin DNR dam records (removed / not on landscape), via the PC thread
pinev: DNR dam point in SW NE sec. 5; the 1917 history gives the same section for the Holcomb dam.

new.pl: On Hwy 70 about 16 miles east of Park Falls, by Riley Creek (Price Co.)
new.v: 1930s coins, CCC buttons and insignia, mess-hall and tool losses
new.st: Price County history pages (WIGenWeb) list the Riley Creek CCC camp, Company 642, 1933-37, 16 miles east of Park Falls on Hwy 70. The 1941 USGS Pike Lake 15-minute topo prints 'Riley Creek CCC Camp' on Hwy 70 at this spot, about 1.2 km south of the GNIS Riley Creek point.
new.t: CCC camps had barracks rows, a mess hall, a rec hall and dumps at the edge of the woods. This is national forest land, so check the rules before digging.
src: Price County WIGenWeb history pages (recovered from the Wayback Machine)
pinev: Read off the 1941 topo label, good to about 100 m (Ground check).
